title: Hotpatch + Containment Protocol for Dedicated Capacity Scaling Regressions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
During a mid-February production surge on dedicated pools, several customers experienced sustained tail latency increases and reduced effective throughput when autoscaler attempted to scale. We observed a transient controller regression that caused oscillations between scale-up and partial teardown paths for GPU allocation pools. This ticket captures the emergency containment steps we took, the diagnostic findings, and the follow-up action items and owners for long-term fixes and guarantees.

Impact: 
- Affected: 14 dedicated customer pools across two regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1).
- Symptoms: Elevated p50/p95 latency, repeated allocation failures in autoscaler logs, and 8% request loss from queue timeouts over a 2 hour window.
- Customer impact: medium (no data corruption, degraded SLA for some routes; some clients routed to fallbacks).

Immediate actions taken (chronological):
1) 2026-02-17 22:05 UTC - Pager triggered by SLO alert (p95 latency > SLA threshold).
2) 22:12 - Triage call (on-call, infra lead, runtime lead). Observed autoscaler decision loops in controller logs correlated with a recent rollout of autoscaler v2.3.1.
3) 22:25 - Applied emergency gate: pinned affected customer pools to older autoscaler image (v2.2.8) to stop oscillations.
4) 22:40 - Increased headroom guard for all dedicated pools by +15% to create breathing room for draining and reallocation.
5) 23:05 - Enabled per-pool circuit-breaker that rejects non-critical background batch workloads to conserve capacity for latency-sensitive serving.
6) 23:50 - Monitored metrics for stabilization; p95 returned toward baseline within 35 minutes for most pools.

Root cause analysis (working hypothesis):
- A throttling backoff introduced in autoscaler v2.3.1 interacts poorly with a new placement optimizer when node reclaim events are frequent. The optimizer requested aggressive bin-packing that reduced free slots; the backoff delayed new allocations causing the controller to requeue scale decisions repeatedly, resulting in oscillation and temporary capacity shortfall.
- Contributing factors: missing regression test for high-reclaim/frequent-eviction scenarios and limited observability on intermediate allocation state in controller traces.

Evidence and artifacts:
- Controller logs (link): https://governance.redwood/incident/ENG-130999/logs (redacted link)
- Autoscaper rollout PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/4012
- Hotfix PR (rollback pin): https://github.com/redwood-inference/deployments/pull/4020
- Temporary dashboard snapshot: https://dash.redwood/incident/130999/snapshot

Immediate remediation checklist (done):
- Rollback/pin autoscaler for affected pools (owner: Marco Li)
- Increase headroom guard and enable emergency batch rejections (owner: SRE rotation)
- Notify impacted customers and route them to fallback models where appropriate (owner: Solutions Eng)

Short-term follow-ups (next 2 weeks):
- Stabilize autoscaler run in canary region with synthetic reclaim load to reproduce oscillation (owner: Runtime Performance, due 2026-02-28).
- Add controller-level allocation tracing to expose reason codes for allocation failures (owner: Infra Observability, due 2026-03-04).
- Create automated smoke test that stresses frequent node reclaim + placement optimizer interleaving (owner: QE, estimate 5).

Long-term action items (quarter roadmap):
- Harden autoscaler decision logic with damping window and hysteresis tied to allocation-state signals (owner: Autoscaler team, release: autoscaler-2.4).
- Add SLO-aware routing policy to preferentially route critical tenants off pooled best-effort queues when headroom < X% (owner: Routing & Policies team).
- Formalize dedicated-capacity canary matrix and pre-merge validation for placement optimizer changes (owner: Platform Reliability).
- Postmortem and lessons learned doc to be published to Confluence and summarized to customers (owner: Incident Commander).

Acceptance criteria for final closure: 
- Reproducible failure mode verified in staging with test harness.
- Autoscaler patch merged with unit and system tests covering reclaim-heavy scenarios.
- New allocation tracing deployed and dashboards updated.
- External postmortem published and customers notified with mitigation recommendations.

Owners: 
- Incident Commander: Aisha Kapoor
- Hotfix/containment: Marco Li
- Observability: Priya Menon
- QE/Test harness: Daniel Reyes
- Customer comms: Nora Fischer
